text:
maya: Heads up — onboarding a HF-derived model into Redwood; tool-calling JSON mode is failing in our evals. Repro steps in-thread.

arjun: I reproduced locally. After int4 quant the tokenizer splits the tool sentinel into two tokens and our parser chokes. Example:
```
# python repl
>>> tokenizer.encode('{\"tool\": \"search\"}\n')
[1012, 3401, 9, 777]  # actual (split sentinel)
# expected a single sentinel id near the end
```
Looks like HF's `additional_special_tokens` were applied differently during conversion — IDs shifted.

sam: Likely cause: quantization + tokenizer merges changed the BPE table ordering, so special token IDs changed if we didn't pin them in the conversion. Did the conversion script emit a `special_tokens_map.json`?

maya: here's the config excerpt we got from the HF bundle we converted:
```json
{"special_tokens": {"bos_token": "<|bos|>", "eos_token": "<|eos|>", "additional_special_tokens": ["<|tool_start|>", "<|tool_end|>", "<|json_mode|>"]}}
```
But when we load into the runtime, RW expects role tokens like `\u0001role_system` / `role_user` (internal names) and exact token ids for JSON-mode sentinels. Those expectations aren't guaranteed by HF bundles.

arjun: Minimal conversion fix I hacked: when converting HF tokenizer -> RW tokenizer, remap/add reserved RW tokens before saving vocab so IDs are stable. Pseudocode:
```python
# pseudo-conversion
hf_tok = load_hf_tokenizer(path)
rw_reserved = {"<|rw_tool_start|>": "__RW_TOOL_START__", "<|rw_json_mode|>": "__RW_JSON_MODE__"}
# ensure reserved tokens occupy top-level slots before merges
hf_tok.add_special_tokens(list(rw_reserved.values()))
hf_tok.save_pretrained(dst)
```
This makes ids deterministic across quantization runs.

lia: We're seeing real eval impact: parsing accuracy down ~12% on toolcall eval suite after this conversion + int4 quant path. Suggest adding a CI check `toolcall-token-id-stability` that runs the converted tokenizer + tiny quant model on a fixed prompt set and asserts sentinel sequences appear as single tokens. Also canary the model before wide rollout.

sam: As a runtime mitigation we could accept both token-level and string-level detection for tool tags: i.e., if token sequence isn't the exact sentinel id, fall back to scanning the decoded string for `\"tool\"` patterns. Ugly, but buys time.

maya: I will open PR to: (1) pin reserved RW tokens during conversion, (2) emit `special_tokens_map.json` mapping HF->RW tokens, and (3) add the token-id-stability CI. Tagging @arjun and @lia for review. :pray:

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: infra/canary/hf-conversion-fix - 2024-05-14T09:30:00Z

ops-bot: playbook created: `tokenizer-migration` and linked to #incidents. Please paste reproduction commands there.

arjun: one more log indicator to watch: `parse_error: unexpected token <int>` coming from the toolcall parser — that'll be the split sentinel signature.

lia: fallback plan if token-id pinning doesn't stabilize: run the toolcall parser on post-decoded strings (not token-level hooks) for the affected models. That will increase latency for tool calls but preserves correctness.

maya: thanks all — PR incoming in ~4h, will add small reproducer and test vectors in the repo.
